text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert NV on Thursday sought to reassure investors that "Kevlar" fibres developed by DuPont De Nemours & Co posed no serious threat to its steel cord products.
"I would like to make it clear that the potential threat from aramid (Kevlar) is no greater today than before," Bekaert chief executive officer Raf Decaluwe told a news conference.

Bekaert's share plunged five percent last December after DuPont began promoting Kevlar fibres for use in reinforcing tyres, claiming they offered weight saving advantages over traditional steel cord products.

At a news conference on Bekaert's 1996 results, Decaluwe said the potential weight saving by using aramid fibres such as Kevlar in an eight kilogramme tyre was 500 grammes, but that the cost was four times greater.
"If you count at normal aramid prices, justifying future investments for expansion, then aramid as a tyre reinforcing material is as much as 10 times more expensive than steel cord," Decaluwe said.

He added that if aramid did ever pose a real threat to steel cord it would cost the tyre industry much time and money to make the switch. "As of today, the new tyre plants being built are based on steel cord technology," he claimed.
